title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Risk Basics
learningObjectives: Explain the core ideas and terminology of dependency and supply-chain risk basics.
Recognize the risks or mistakes this topic is intended to prevent.
Apply appropriate defensive practices in a beginner project.
Distinguish this topic from related security concepts and controls.
Review a simple design and justify improvements using evidence.

understand.concept: Software supply-chain risk includes compromised or malicious dependencies, typosquatted packages, unmaintained components, vulnerable versions, build tooling, and unexpected updates. Reduce risk by choosing trusted sources, reviewing package names and maintainers, minimizing dependencies, pinning or locking versions, monitoring advisories, and verifying changes. Dependency checks help but do not guarantee safety.
understand.whyItMatters: A project inherits risk from tools and components it uses, not only from its own source code.
understand.analogy: Think of a careful community space where entry, use of shared items, and privacy are guided by clear rules and appropriate checks.
understand.analogyLimit: Software security depends on technical boundaries, data flows, implementation details, and changing threats that this analogy cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative:
Software supply-chain risk includes compromised or malicious dependencies, typosquatted packages, unmaintained components, vulnerable versions, build tooling, and unexpected updates. Reduce risk by choosing trusted sources, reviewing package names and maintainers, minimizing dependencies, pinning or locking versions, monitoring advisories, and verifying changes. Dependency checks help but do not guarantee safety.

Apply these principles proportionately. Use established platform and library protections instead of improvising security-critical mechanisms. For a real application, confirm requirements and review the implementation with qualified peers.

commonMistakes: Assuming a feature is safe because it works in normal use.
Trusting client-side controls as the only enforcement.
Applying one generic transformation to every kind of input or output.
Exposing credentials or personal data in source, logs, or screenshots.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Write a dependency policy for a small project. Include approval criteria, lockfile use, update cadence, advisory response, and steps for replacing an unmaintained package.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy project and no real secrets or personal data.
Write a dependency policy for a small project. Include approval criteria, lockfile use, update cadence, advisory response, and steps for replacing an unmaintained package.
Explain the decisions you made and limitations.
Identify at least one test or review step.
